reason: Parked by the agreed hard stop of the funded stage 'tight' (2026-10-11): the leading-spacer recovery lemma is not proved. Proved in the stage (informally, on validated unit rules): a closed form TF of when a leading-spacer eat word keeps a t (one bit pattern per layout; exact on all 265,642 words to 13 units and 103,000 long random or constructed words), the exact word it produces (bin(C_0) t^a inc(W)[a:]), that the next eat never reaches the surviving t, and that the first unit to reach the new v = 110 unit is a C run, never the B carry. Open: the head after that C-meets-v event (no unit rule; observed real = shadow plus a head) and a bound on how many eats the head survives (observed 1-3, 0 halts in every test). Not a cryptid: tightness is an explicit congruence on the layout and halting never depends on the bits. No further stages.
